models_evaluated: Epic BestPractice Advisory rule-based QT alert (prior QTc>=500 ms)

links.outcome: Drug-induced QT prolongation and mortality before vs after alert deployment
links.effect: Alert identified high-risk patients (OR 2.28, 95% CI 2.10-2.47) but diLQTS risk unchanged after deployment (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.94-1.36); inpatient mortality higher post-deployment (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.09-1.88).
links.quote: We found that despite successful identification of high-risk patients for diLQTS, deployment of an alert-based CDS did not impact the risk of diLQTS.

models_evaluated: Epic BestPractice Advisory: rule-based alert triggered by QT-prolonging medication orders and prior QTc ≥500 milliseconds

links.outcome: Drug-induced long QT syndrome after versus before CDS implementation
links.effect: CDS deployment did not significantly reduce diLQTS (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.94-1.36; P =.21), with no evidence of an effect for individual medications (P =.98).
links.quote: After adjustment for age, sex, race and ethnicity, location, laboratory findings, medication, and comorbidity clusters, there was no difference in risk of diLQTS based on CDS deployment (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.94-1.36; P =.21; Table S10A in Multimedia Appendix 1 ), and no evidence of effect for any individual medication ( P =.98; Table S10B in Multimedia Appendix 1 ).

links.effect: deployment of the alert-based CDS did not impact the risk of diLQTS despite accurate risk prediction
links.quote: We found that despite successful identification of high-risk patients for diLQTS, deployment of an alert-based CDS did not impact the risk of diLQTS.

links.effect: the risk of diLQTS was not significantly different, and mortality was significantly higher after deployment
links.quote: When compared with rates prior to implementation, the risk of diLQTS was not significantly different after the CDS tools were deployed across the system, although mortality was significantly higher after the tools were implemented.

links.effect: successful identification of high-risk patients did not translate to reduced clinical risk in practice
links.quote: We found that despite successful identification of high-risk patients for diLQTS, deployment of an alert-based CDS did not impact the risk of diLQTS.
